headers.//: Hashed build assets. Vite writes the content hash into the filename, so index-BDeGAHmo.js is that exact bytes and nothing else — the name changes when the content does. A file that can never go stale should never be revalidated. Vercel's default served these with max-age=0, must-revalidate, which made every kiosk re-check ~780KB over shop WiFi before it could paint.

The HTML must NEVER be immutable. It is the only unhashed file, so it is the thing that tells a kiosk which hashed bundle to load — and the update check reads it to detect a new build. Cache it and the fleet stops updating. This restates Vercel's current default explicitly so that a future change cannot silently break the update mechanism.
